roster_group_notes: Demiurg commerce vessels share several traits: Ponderous (no Come to New Heading); heavily automated, starting each battle at a fixed Ld rather than rolling; an armoured 6+ prow; Absorber/Repulsor Fields (they never suffer a speed penalty for being in contact with blast markers, are immune to the effects of solar flares, radiation bursts, and gas/dust clouds, and never gain blast markers due to any type of celestial phenomena; when a Demiurg vessel moves, it must collect every blast marker touched by its base during its movement, removing them from the table and setting them aside in a separate pile for that vessel; markers in contact when it begins its move are collected immediately and so do not affect its leadership if it attempts a command check, but command checks made at other times are still affected normally); and, in two specific circumstances only, a higher victory-point value when destroyed (see Demiurg VP below). Each commerce vessel begins each battle with a nominal Ld value (shown in its notes) rather than rolling randomly. For each point of damage it suffers thereafter, it reduces its Ld value by 1 for the remainder of the battle, to a minimum of Ld5. If it suffers a 'Bridge Smashed!' critical result, it suffers one extra point of damage rather than the usual -3 Ld penalty. The Cutting Beam is a lance (15cm, Front): base firepower 1, +1 per blast marker the ship collected in its preceding movement phase, to a maximum of firepower 8 (shown as FP1+). Alternatively, two markers may be expended to increase the cutting beam's range to 30cm (with the rest contributing to its firepower). Unused markers are lost at the end of each turn. Demiurg attack craft are Fighters (ASF, 30cm), Bombers (BMR, 20cm), and Assault Boats (AB, 30cm). Mercenaries: unless a fleet is composed entirely of Demiurg vessels, they are considered to be hired mercenaries. In this case, Demiurg ships will not continue to fight after becoming crippled, instead attempting to disengage each and every turn thereafter, or moving as fast as possible towards the nearest table edge if they fail, until they have successfully left the board. However, such is the Demiurg's hatred for the Orks that if the opposing fleet includes any Ork vessels, Demiurg ships will not begin attempting to disengage until they have 2 or fewer hit points remaining, rather than when they are crippled. Hired Reserves: any fleet except Orks, Tyranids, and Necrons may substitute Bastion or Citadel commerce vessels in place of any reserve cruisers it is normally allowed. They follow the normal rules for reserves and allies of convenience, and are still subject to the Mercenaries rule.

armament_raw: Macrobatteries 30cm FP12 (L), (R); Lances 60cm FP3 (L), (R); Prow Macrobatteries 45cm FP14 (F); Prow Cutting Beam 15cm FP1+ (F); Dorsal Torps 30cm S6 (All Round); Dorsal Launch Bays S3 (BMR 20cm)
